Keep useful Rust/CUDA/CuTile code, exact packed top-k/tie semantics, clean packages, bounded resources and reproducible tests; no paper-only result. Preserve all current Sfora work, consultations and DGX jobs, inspect before launching, and do not duplicate. Current verified exploratory anchors: three-seed public-config SOP official TEST packed R@1 91.7419% versus dated UNICOM 91.2%, but TEST was previously observed and no matched full-pipeline speed win exists; older three-seed In-Shop official query/gallery packed R@1 95.4823% versus UNICOM 96.7%, while the newer true-freeze checkpoint has no official result. Its TRAIN holdout diagnostic got 97.6235% on 6,354 queries, but this is not an official or scale-projected result; impostor-count misses are sublinear, so the linear scaling premise failed. The selected SOP batch-1 p99 diagnostic was 19.622 versus 19.606 ms, not a speed win; batch-32 global thread reduction failed p99. CUB transfer gain is positive, Cars transfer inconclusive. Treat all these as evidence, not SOTA claims. Diagnose the concrete In-Shop quality gap and the public image-to-result latency bottleneck from existing receipts; pick ONE cheapest causally distinct TRAIN-only intervention, with a predeclared stop rule, instead of another series of unbounded probes or loss tweaks. Consider representation, architecture, data coverage, sampling, supervision, training algorithm, compression, preprocessing and serving; use psychology/physics/other-field inspiration only when it yields a testable mechanism. Freeze method and checkpoint selection on TRAIN identities; compare matched backbone, data, compute budget, scorer and paired seeds, report R@1/mAP@R and class/query uncertainty. Qualify both official protocols, plus CUB and Cars transfer, distinguishing exploratory official reads from new independent confirmation. Preserve actual packed-score quality; exact output parity is mandatory for kernel changes. Measure training time, images/s and VRAM and full decode/preprocess/encoder/packing/native-search/image-to-top-k p50/p95/p99 and QPS at batch1 and batch32, same hardware and query/gallery. A p99 product claim needs 10,000 interleaved paired calls and a confidence interval. Run GPU work only on authenticated DGX Spark after cheaper local/CPU falsifiers, with raw receipts and cost. Use Opus 5.5 plus GPT-6 Astra for consequential critique and Fable for truly new research, without duplicate jobs. If either quality or speed fails, change the responsible layer and stop negative arms early. Within 24 hours push a substantive library/training increment and concise verified decision table with datasets, splits, controls, quality, speed, uncertainty and next gate; continue until the production joint quality-and-speed target is met.

reviewers.partial_result:
**Verdict: this is a cheap, action-bearing mechanics gate and worth running, but not as written.** One of its frozen caps is already contradicted by the repository's own evidence. If it launched as-is, the gate would most likely STOP on the control arm, and under the gate's no-rescue rule that would block PE for a reason unrelated to PE.

I edited nothing. The protected `topk.rs` SHA is still `1ae7f50a…b587` and the file is still modified and unstaged.

## Mandatory before implementing or launching

1. **The 10 GB peak CUDA cap is impossible for the Large arm.** `inshop-unseen-freeze-179025-smoke17-v2.json` records Large/256 with `frozen_encoder_blocks` 0–11 on a GB10 at batch 64 in BF16, and its `training_peak_cuda_allocated_bytes` is **16,940,154,368** (about 16.9 GB). The new gate uses the same configuration, plus a second model resident in the process, under a cap below 10 GB. So the gate is set up to fail on the control arm, not on PE. Before freezing the gate:
   - give each arm its own cap: keep PE below 10 GB, and set Large from that 16.9 GB measurement plus a stated margin;
   - reset peak memory stats before each arm and free the first arm's model, optimizer and cache before starting the second;
   - record a peak for each arm.

   Setting these caps before launch corrects the design. It is not the kind of cap enlargement after failure that the gate forbids.
2. **Host memory headroom under 8 GiB is untested.** The pilot's peak was 2.95 GB (inference only, FP16 autocast). The trainer's parent process peaked at 6.68 GB with one model. This run adds two FP32 models, AdamW state and two pixel caches: 1024 images at 224 and at 256 come to about 1.4 GB as FP32, or about 0.35 GB as uint8. Store pixels as uint8, reuse the pilot's FP32 loaders (these kept RSS at 2.95 GB) rather than the trainer's `AutoModel` path, and have the CPU dry run record RSS after both models and the pixel caches are loaded. Alternatively, run the arms as two serial locked processes, which also removes cross-arm contamination of memory and timing.
3. **The GPU run cannot demonstrate the duplicate-refresh rule.** With no augmentation, the two repeated copies of an image have identical pixels, so the first and last occurrence give the same features. "Last duplicate wins" can only be demonstrated by the CPU fixture using distinct values. The receipt must say so and must not cite the GPU run as evidence for it.
4. **Frozen-integrity hashes must cover `state_dict()`, not only `named_parameters()`, and the gradient check must be per parameter.** A single norm per block can hide a dead tensor. Report any zero-gradient trainable parameter by name. In PE that means the `attn_pool` probe, attention, norm and MLP, plus `ln_post`, `proj` and every tail block. In Large it means `head.*`, `post_layernorm` and `layers[12:]`. Also assert that exactly the frozen inventory has `grad is None`. This matters because the trainer passes all of `vision.parameters()` to AdamW and relies on AdamW skipping parameters whose `.grad` is `None`.
5. **Record the FP16-cache versus BF16-training difference at step 1 from data you already produce.** Before the optimizer runs, compute the cosine between each refreshed bank row and its cached FP16 row. That is the numerical profile the spec asks for, at no extra cost. Also apply the first-four BF16 vs FP32 cosine guard (≥ 0.999) to Large, not just PE. Loading Large directly in FP32 and running it under BF16 is also a new path.

## Checked and sound

- **`scripts/pe_core_training.py` (untracked):** it calls `vision.requires_grad_(True)` and then re-freezes `rope`. `rope.freqs` is natively `requires_grad=False` (`learned_freq=False`), so the final state is correct.
- **PE-B16 config:** it has no LayerScale, no drop_path and no grad checkpointing, so freezing a prefix in train mode is deterministic.
- **Bank positives:** `member_bank_positive_ordinals` excludes each image's own row, so every anchor has exactly one positive in the bank (the product's other image). That is not degenerate.
- **Wall-clock budget:** the Large smoke's median step was 1.01 s, including augmentation and data loading, so 16+16 steps plus loading should fit in 180 s.

## Advisory, not blocking

- The ≤ 0.8 step-time ratio is close to certain to pass: pilot encoder time was 70 ms vs 263 ms, and Large runs 12 trainable blocks against PE's 6. It carries little information, but it costs nothing and is honestly labelled as a cost check.
- Fix the arm order in advance and record it. The pilot alternated calls; this run is serial.
- A BF16 cosine or finiteness failure should be recorded as a closed **precision configuration**, not as evidence against PE. The FVCG bf16 VJP-parity failure is a precedent for an instrument failure being misread as a method failure. The doc's "stops this configuration" wording already allows this; keep that framing in the result doc.

The PASS-licenses-a-proposal, no-quality-claim scope is right. With corrections 1 and 2 fixed before freezing, the gate is sound to launch once.

Keep useful Rust/CUDA/CuTile code, exact packed top-k/tie semantics, clean packages, bounded resources and reproducible tests; no paper-only result. Preserve all current Sfora work, consultations and DGX jobs, inspect before launching, and do not duplicate. Current verified exploratory anchors: three-seed public-config SOP official TEST packed R@1 91.7419% versus dated UNICOM 91.2%, but TEST was previously observed and no matched full-pipeline speed win exists; older three-seed In-Shop official query/gallery packed R@1 95.4823% versus UNICOM 96.7%, while the newer true-freeze checkpoint has no official result. Its TRAIN holdout diagnostic got 97.6235% on 6,354 queries, but this is not an official or scale-projected result; impostor-count misses are sublinear, so the linear scaling premise failed. The selected SOP batch-1 p99 diagnostic was 19.622 versus 19.606 ms, not a speed win; batch-32 global thread reduction failed p99. CUB transfer gain is positive, Cars transfer inconclusive. Treat all these as evidence, not SOTA claims. Diagnose the concrete In-Shop quality gap and the public image-to-result latency bottleneck from existing receipts; pick ONE cheapest causally distinct TRAIN-only intervention, with a predeclared stop rule, instead of another series of unbounded probes or loss tweaks. Consider representation, architecture, data coverage, sampling, supervision, training algorithm, compression, preprocessing and serving; use psychology/physics/other-field inspiration only when it yields a testable mechanism. Freeze method and checkpoint selection on TRAIN identities; compare matched backbone, data, compute budget, scorer and paired seeds, report R@1/mAP@R and class/query uncertainty. Qualify both official protocols, plus CUB and Cars transfer, distinguishing exploratory official reads from new independent confirmation. Preserve actual packed-score quality; exact output parity is mandatory for kernel changes. Measure training time, images/s and VRAM and full decode/preprocess/encoder/packing/native-search/image-to-top-k p50/p95/p99 and QPS at batch1 and batch32, same hardware and query/gallery. A p99 product claim needs 10,000 interleaved paired calls and a confidence interval. Run GPU work only on authenticated DGX Spark after cheaper local/CPU falsifiers, with raw receipts and cost. Use Opus 5.5 plus GPT-6 Astra for consequential critique and Fable for truly new research, without duplicate jobs. If either quality or speed fails, change the responsible layer and stop negative arms early. Within 24 hours push a substantive library/training increment and concise verified decision table with datasets, splits, controls, quality, speed, uncertainty and next gate; continue until the production joint quality-and-speed target is met.

reviewers.partial_result:
**Yes: this is a supported, bounded mechanics gate. It is not launch-ready yet.** The source evidence supports testing trainability and update cost; it does not establish learned quality or serving speed. I verified the saved feature archive’s hash and the native PE source hashes against the pilot authorities.

Mandatory corrections:

1. **P1 — The new freeze helper crashes on native PE, and its fixture hides the bug.**  
   [pe_core_training.py](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/pe_core_training.py:13) calls `vision.rope.requires_grad_(False)`. Native [`Rope2D`](/tmp/sfora-pe-source/core/vision_encoder/rope.py:303) is a plain Python object without that method; its nested `rope` is the module. The fixture substitutes `nn.Linear`, so it cannot detect this failure. Freeze and audit the nested frequency parameter explicitly, verify the shared RoPE references across blocks, and use a faithful fixture. Ordinary `vision.named_parameters()` and the existing parameter digest omit this unregistered object. Preserve the native 163-key checkpoint authority; do not change module registration to work around the audit.

2. **P1 — Define and measure the claimed FP16-cache/BF16 numerical bound.**  
   The [gate](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/inshop_pe_training_smoke_gate_2026-09-28.md:14) says to bound that difference, but its only numerical criterion compares PE BF16 against FP32. The [plan](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-pe-training-mechanics.md:24) incorrectly presents that as the cache comparison. Before updates, compare aligned cached FP16-source rows with fresh BF16 outputs for **both arms**, using a predeclared subset and bound. Retain the separate PE BF16/FP32 ≥0.999 guard. Report projected/readout differences without claiming exact initial bank parity.

3. **P1 — Make finiteness checks cover every update and the final post-update state.**  
   [“Check at first and last step”](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/inshop_pe_training_smoke_gate_2026-09-28.md:42) is appropriate for detailed route diagnostics, but insufficient as the complete finiteness contract. Require finite losses and preclip gradients every step, then finite parameters, optimizer state and refreshed bank after each update—including step 16. The [existing trainer](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/scripts/train_inshop_siglip2_unseen_gallery.py:1298) already checks these states. Define the named gradient/hash groups explicitly: each tail block, each applicable post-normalization/pooling/projection group, head and classifier. An aggregate vision hash changing cannot establish that every required group updated.

4. **P2 — Freeze an unambiguous timing statistic before launch.**  
   [The cost rule](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/docs/inshop_pe_training_smoke_gate_2026-09-28.md:49) requests forward/backward/update timings but does not specify which total supplies the ≤0.8 ratio. Define synchronized step boundaries and explicitly include or exclude transfer, objective, clipping, bank refresh and diagnostics identically for both arms. Use `median(PE total steps 3–16) / median(Large total steps 3–16)`; keep component timings descriptive. Keep hashing outside the measured step interval, while retaining it inside the whole-process cap. Specify CUDA’s exact byte ceiling and retain initialization in peak accounting.

5. **P2 — State the actual update coverage.**  
   With the [existing sampler](/home/rb/worktrees/sfora-positive-causality/src/sfora/unicom_rank_finish.py:12), 64 slots with four slots/product gives 16 products/step. Sixteen coverage-first steps therefore exercise **256 distinct products and 512 distinct images**, with 1,024 image presentations. All 1,024 images still initialize PCA/proxies/bank. Record these separate counts and freeze the sampler’s `epoch`, which affects its RNG. This is acceptable for mechanics; it must not be described as updating all 512 products.

The duplicate-refresh specification is correct: the existing helper selects the last occurrence and stores detached normalized **pre-update** outputs after the optimizer step.

Proceed with implementation after these corrections, then review the concrete executable and bounded launcher before the single run. No larger budget or architecture change is warranted by these findings. I made no edits, ran no GPU/training/download work, and sent no messages or consultations. The protected Rust SHA-256 matches the supplied value.
